title: Redwood cost econ discovery with Golden Bridge Capital
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private, batching/caching levers, quantization tradeoffs, and a conservative POC budget. Customer wants a pilot to validate unit costs on their 25M tokens/month workload and understands fallbacks and SLAs.
topics: dedicated reserved vs hosted (burst) cost tradeoffs
next_steps: Jamal to send a tailored pricing spreadsheet with sample cost model by 2026-03-06
Sofia to schedule a 2-hour technical deep-dive and throughput benchmark slot week of 3/9
Customer to share a sample prompt distribution and token histogram by 3/5
Set up trial account for Golden Bridge with 30-day pilot quota
action_items: Jamal: Email pricing spreadsheet and high-level cost assumptions (due 2026-03-06)
Sofia: Coordinate benchmark window and provide Redwood benchmark checklist (due 2026-03-09)
Ethan: Share prompt samples and token distribution CSV (due 2026-03-05)
Noah: Confirm budget band and procurement timeline (due 2026-03-10)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~42 min
Attendees: Jamal Price (Redwood AE), Sofia Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Li (Golden Bridge - Head of ML), Marisa Gomez (Eng Manager), Noah Patel (FinOps), Oliver Chen (Data Ops)

Summary: quick intro, then deep dive on unit economics, followed by agreement on POC next steps. Some audio glitches and a couple of overlapped speakers, transcription has minor mis-hears.

00:00 Jamal: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:04 Ethan: yep good here, thanks Jamal.
00:10 Jamal: quick intros, i'll kick off — i'm jamal, AE at Redwood, and with me is sofia, our se.
00:17 Sofia: hi hi folks, i'll focus on the benchmarks and runtime questions.
00:21 Marisa: marisa here, we own the app infra that will call the LLM.
00:25 Noah: noah, i'll be watching the finances and budget constraints.
00:29 Jamal: great. objective for today is to understand your usage profile, what matters for cost, and figure out a pilot that validates unit economics.

01:02 Ethan: high-level, we run a recommender + summaries pipeline, approx 25 million tokens per month today and growing. Latency SLO is 300-500ms p95 for interactive features, and for nightly batch jobs latency is not critical. We are sensitive to cost — expected to cap at "X" in Q2, which noah will detail.

01:28 Noah: right, we have a $10k/month trial bump and then need to align on unit costs to see if it fits forward budget. If per-token is too high for live calls we can't proceed.

01:50 Sofia: helpful — can you share a token histogram? distribution across short prompts vs long chaining?
01:55 Ethan: yep will share — most calls are short, 80% under 120 tokens, but we have a tail for summaries 1-2k tokens.

02:18 Jamal: ok so two levers to look at: per-token pricing for hosted usage, batching + prefix/KV caching to reduce effective tokens, and dedicated reserved capacity which changes unit economics. we'll walk through examples.

02:42 Sofia: i'll add that quantization (8-bit/4-bit) and model choice are big factors — we can recommend a model family that meets your quality bar but reduces token cost by improving throughput per GPU.

03:05 Marisa: can you explain how caching works in Hosted? i heard about KV cache and also prefix cache, what's the difference?

03:14 Sofia: yeah, so Prefix caching is when you have repeated prompts or instructions — like a system prompt or template — we can cache the prefix embeddings so you don't re-send tokens to be computed each time, that reduces tokens billed in practice. KV cache refers to the transformer key/value cache for long-running conversations; it saves compute on the model side but depending on how the provider bills it may still count initial tokens. In Redwood's hosted we do automatic prefix caching and offer options for persistent KV caching for sessions — it's a little messy in billing across providers so we show an "effective tokens" metric.

03:58 Noah: how do you show effective tokens? like do you give us a modeled monthly spend?

04:06 Jamal: yes, we build a sample cost model: raw tokens x per-token rate, then subtract cached-savings and batching efficiency. For example: if 80% calls are 100 tokens and batching gives 1.8x efficiency on generation tokens, your effective tokens could drop ~30-40%.

04:28 Ethan: what's the per-token rate for hosted? and how much discount on dedicated?

04:33 Jamal: nominal hosted open-model pricing — we gave ballpark ranges in the deck earlier. For the pilot we'll send a tailored spreadsheet. Roughly: hosted per-token might be $0.0009 to $0.0018 per token depending on model/throughput; dedicated reserved capacity looks at cost per GPU-hour and your throughput — effective per-token could be 30-60% lower at steady state, but you need a commit. numbers vary by model size.

05:05 Sofia: and importantly batching affects inference throughput. With dedicated you can tune batch sizes and concurrency to hit your latency SLO while maximizing tokens/sec. On hosted we do continuous batching but there's limits for ultra-low-latency.

05:22 Marisa: can we get a clear worked example for our 25M tokens?

05:27 Jamal: sure. example slide: assume 25M raw tokens/month. Without caching and naive hosted rate at $0.0012 = $30k/month. If caching + batching gives 35% effective reduction you end up 16.25M effective tokens -> $19.5k/month. If you go dedicated and commit to reserved GPUs you'll see effective token rate drop further — say to $0.0006 -> $9k/month plus reserved infra fee. So order-of-magnitude: hosted pilot 15-25k, dedicated at scale potentially sub-10k.

06:05 Noah: ok that's promising but we need firm numbers for procurement. Also curious about burst and fallbacks — if dedicated is full do you spill to hosted and what's the cost implication?

06:18 Sofia: yes we support hybrid routing: dedicated primary, hosted fallback. Fallback is billed at hosted rates plus a small routing fee. We can cap fallback usage to avoid surprise bills. For the pilot we'll show a routing policy example.

06:35 Ethan: what about quality drift with quantized models? we can't lose summary quality.

06:41 Sofia: fair point — we recommend running evals on your prompt set. For many workloads 8-bit quantization preserves quality; 4-bit sometimes needs evals. We'll run A/Bs during the benchmark window and measure ROUGE/embedding similarity.

07:02 Marisa: do you have telemetry for token-level cost per route? i want per-endpoint dashboards.

07:08 Jamal: yep Redwood Console gives per-route/token cost, latency breakdowns, and traces. We'll include sample screenshots.

07:22 Oliver: security: can we run Private (VPC) with KMS?

07:27 Sofia: yes, Private supports VPC+KMS/HSM and we ship audit logs. There is higher op overhead and a different pricing profile; usually chosen for compliance reasons not pure cost.

07:40 Ethan: timeline: we want to decide by end of March whether to move to a Q2 pilot. what's realistic?

07:46 Jamal: sounds reasonable — pilot in mid-march, two weeks of benchmarking with your traffic replayed and then a short cost validation period.

08:02 Noah: procurement question — if we commit to dedicated capacity what's typical contract length and termination?
08:08 Jamal: typical reserved is 12 months with quarterly billing; minimum commitments can be flexible for pilots; we can discuss a 3-month reserved pilot for the POC.
08:28 Ethan: any red flags you see in our profile?
08:31 Sofia: only tail latencies for the 1-2k token summaries — that'll need dedicated tuning or async batch flows. Also need to instrument to capture effective tokens and caching stats; if you don't capture that you'll mis-estimate savings.
08:48 Marisa: for benchmarks what do you need from us?
08:52 Sofia: 1) sample prompts + token histogram, 2) a replay script or recordings for 24-48h of representative traffic, 3) quality eval set for summaries. We'll provide a benchmark checklist.
09:06 Jamal: ok quick recap and next steps — we'll send pricing sheet, request the prompt samples, sofia schedules the benchmark, set up trial account. Any other questions?
09:18 Ethan: none here. thanks.
09:22 Noah: please flag any assumptions in the pricing sheet — e.g., network egress, storage for KV cache, and model variant.
09:30 Jamal: will do. thanks everyone.
End of call.
